title: Sum with a moving pointer
description:
Write `sum(first, last)`. `first` points at the first `int` of a run of ints, and `last` points **one past** the final one. It returns the total of all of them.

For an array `int values[4]{ 10, 20, 30, 40 };` the call is `sum(values, values + 4)` and the answer is 100.

When `first` and `last` are equal the run is empty and the total is 0.

Walk a pointer along the memory. Square brackets are not allowed in this task.
hints: `last` is never dereferenced. It is only there to compare against, so the loop knows where to stop.
The loop keeps going while the moving pointer is not equal to `last`: `p != last`.
`++p` moves a pointer to the next `int`, and `*p` is the value it is currently pointing at.
`first` and `last` are pointers to `const int`, so the pointer you walk with has to be a `const int*` too.
rules: Use a pointer and `*`, with no square brackets.

rules.message: Use a pointer and `*`, with no square brackets.
